questions.question: Adjustments exist because:
options: The ledger describes the year AS RECORDED, and some year-end truths have no document yet
The trial balance never balances at year end
The owner wants a larger profit
Journals must be rewritten annually

questions.question: The pre-adjustment and post-adjustment trial balances are:
options: Two names for the same document
The ledger as routine left it, and the ledger after the adjustments — the version final accounts are built from
The debit column and the credit column
Last year's and this year's balances

questions.question: The engine behind every adjustment is:
options: Historical cost
The business entity rule
The MATCHING principle — this year's statement must carry this year's incomes and expenses, no more, no less
Double taxation

questions.question: Prudence demands that a discovered loss be recognised:
options: When the owner approves it
Only if it exceeds R1 000
In the following year
The moment it is discovered — not when convenient

questions.question: Stationery shows R1 000; R200 sits unused at year end. The adjustment is:
options: Credit Stationery R200, debit Consumable Stores on Hand R200 — expense reports the R800 used; the asset carries the rest forward
Debit Stationery R200, credit Bank R200
Credit Stationery R800, debit Trading Stock R800
No entry — stationery is always fully expensed

questions.question: Trading Stock claims R2 400; the stocktake counts R2 250. The books must:
options: Adjust the count upward to R2 400
Come down to the count — credit Trading Stock R150, debit Trading Stock Deficit R150
Wait a year to see if the stock returns
Debit Trading Stock R150

questions.question: The Trading Stock Deficit account is:
options: An asset carried to next year
A liability owed to suppliers
An EXPENSE — the recognised loss of stock gone to theft, breakage or error
Part of Cost of Sales

questions.question: After the adjustments, the post-adjustment trial balance still levels because:
options: The bookkeeper forces the totals
Adjustments are recorded outside the ledger
Only debits were adjusted
Every adjustment was itself a full double entry

subtopics.title: The Final Accounts — Trading, and Profit and Loss

questions.question: The Trading account isolates:
options: The buying-and-selling story — Sales against Cost of Sales, its balance the GROSS profit
All expenses of the year
The owner's drawings
The bank reconciliation

questions.question: Sales R100 000 against Cost of Sales R80 000 gives gross profit R20 000, which also confirms:
options: The year's net profit
The 25% mark-up on cost — a quarter of R80 000 is exactly R20 000
The trading stock deficit
The capital balance

questions.question: Into the Profit and Loss account go:
options: Only the gross profit
Assets and liabilities
The gross profit, the other incomes (rent R6 000), and every operating expense — totalling R14 500 on the debit side
The trial balance columns

questions.question: The net profit of R11 500 finally transfers to:
options: Bank
Sales
Trading Stock
Capital — the profit belongs to the owner

questions.question: The correct year-end order is:
options: Pre-adjustment TB → adjustments → post-adjustment TB → final accounts → profit to Capital → statements
Final accounts → adjustments → trial balance → statements
Statements → final accounts → adjustments
Adjustments → pre-adjustment TB → statements → final accounts

questions.question: Preparing final accounts BEFORE adjusting would:
options: Save time with no loss of accuracy
Make the profit wrong by every unadjusted rand — built on unfixed stationery and uncounted stock
Double the gross profit
Be required by prudence

questions.question: The R200 stationery adjustment appears downstream as:
options: One change only, in the expense
A change in Sales
TWO appearances — a smaller expense in Profit and Loss AND an asset in the statements
A creditor to be settled

questions.question: The classic lost mark in this topic is:
options: Naming too many GAAP principles
Using the General Journal for adjustments
Writing narrations
The half-adjustment — recording one side of what must be a full double entry

questions.question: "You cannot photocopy a diary and call it a report card" because:
options: Some diary lines have drifted from the truth — unused stationery, uncounted stock — and must be tidied first
Diaries are private documents
Report cards use different currency
The diary is too long to copy

questions.question: Year-end's two jobs, in strict order, are:
options: Squeeze first, tidy second
TIDY the diary to match the real shop (adjustments), then SQUEEZE it into the report card (final accounts)
Count the cash, then close the shop
Pay the creditors, then the debtors

questions.question: The report card answers the owner's two oldest questions:
options: Who owes us, and whom do we owe?
Which journal is busiest, and which door is fastest?
Did the shop make money this year, and how much?
What is on the shelf, and what is in the till?

subtopics.title: Tidying the Room Before the Photo

questions.question: The R1 000 stationery line splits into:
options: R800 truly USED (stays as expense) and R200 still WAITING (a parcel handed to next year as an asset)
R500 used and R500 wasted
R1 000 expense and R200 extra expense
R200 used and R800 waiting

questions.question: "The shelf wins — always" means:
options: Stock on shelves may not be sold
The physical count is the fact; the books adjust DOWN to it, with the missing R150 admitted as a named loss
The books are adjusted up to R2 400
The shelf is counted only when convenient

questions.question: "Bad news goes on the card immediately; good news waits to be proven" is the home-clothes version of:
options: Matching
Going concern
Prudence
Historical cost

questions.question: "This year's card must carry only this year's using" is the home-clothes version of:
options: Prudence
Business entity
Going concern
Matching

subtopics.title: Two Sieves and the Owner's Jar

questions.question: Sieve one catches the buying-and-selling story and leaves behind:
options: R20 000 — the gross profit, the mark-up's reward before any running cost
R11 500 — the net profit
R14 500 — the running costs
R6 000 — the rent income

questions.question: Sieve two receives R26 000 of earning (gross profit plus rent) and drains R14 500 of running costs, leaving:
options: R11 500 — the net profit, what the year truly earned

questions.question: The net profit lands in the owner's jar — Capital — because:
options: The bank requires it
It must be spent before March
The profit was always the owner's; the shop was working it up all year
Nominal accounts cannot be emptied

questions.question: After the squeeze, the year's nominal pages stand:
options: Carrying their balances into the new year
Doubled for safety
Converted into liabilities
Empty — clean for the new year, their story summarised in the jar
